checks.note: The six-step description matches p72 verbatim.
checks.sentence: The company does not sell a product off a shelf. It wins work through a competitive tender process, and the filing describes the cycle in six steps. The client floats a tender for a specific work or contract. A pre-bid meeting is held to resolve queries. The contractor bids, taking into account its eligibility for that particular contract. The job is awarded to the lowest quote — a letter of acceptance is issued to the lowest bidder. The contractor deposits a security in the form of a performance guarantee. Then drawings are issued and the site is handed over for execution.
checks.supporting_excerpt_quote: Steps involved in Contract Execution: 1) Tender is Floated by client for a specific Work /Contract 2) Pre-Bid Meeting held for discussion and resolving Queries in regard to floated Tender 3) Tender is bidded by Contractor taking into its eligibility for that particular Contract 4) Job /Work is awarded to the lowest Quote – Letter of Acceptance issued to the lowest Bidder 5) Contractor has to deposit Security in form of performance Guarantee for the contact awarded 6) Drawing issued , Site handover for execution of Work

checks.note: The quoted portion matches p12; the surrounding sentences are analytical summary, not new factual claims.
checks.sentence: The draft itself summarises the position in one sentence: "Majority of our revenues will be dependent on one customer, Indian Railways, which is our largest customer, contributing to 57% of our revenue in Fiscal 2018." An investor considering this issue is, in effect, considering a bet on the continued flow of railway contracts to a single Mumbai contractor — with a profit spike in the most recent year that the filing does not explain, and a cash flow position the filing admits has been negative.

report.summary: The report is tightly sourced: nearly every tagged claim matches the cited DRHP page, including all financial figures, customer names, dates, and governance disclosures. Two partial issues need small fixes: the p71 tag does not itself support 'Mumbai-based' or 'government clients' (covered elsewhere), and the p55 description of 'only two stray figures' is imprecise because the page also shows other figures. No unsupported or wrong-source claims were found.
